contents.reason: The weak and strong Morse inequalities are owned by the later Morse-inequalities page of this run; the correspondence and duality results here make no inequality claim.

contents.name: Theorem 5.4.4, introduction of a complementary pair of handles at any point of a decomposition

contents.name: Theorem 5.4.5, the handle addition theorem realising y plus or minus x by deforming an attaching sphere
contents.reason: Handle addition is a slide-type modification owned by the following handle-cancellation page; this pair only reorders and regroups the handles already present.

contents.name: Lemma 5.1.8, infinite handle exhaustions of noncompact manifolds
contents.reason: The selected pair concerns compact cobordisms only; Wall's noncompact exhaustion would need its own page and no item of this pair consumes it.

contents.name: Section 5.4 remarks on orientable and non-orientable 1-handles
contents.reason: The compact cobordism, duality and rearrangement results here are orientation-free and never classify 1-handles by orientability, so this material is not scaffolded.

contents.name: Theorem 5.3.5, Lefschetz and Poincare duality proved through the dual handle decomposition
contents.reason: Poincare-Lefschetz duality is owned by the algebraic-topology track and is not a prerequisite or a claim of any item on this page.
